findings.title: Commit markers are coarser than one-per-task
findings.description: Tasks 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 10 carry no `**Commit**:` of their own; the work of Tasks 4+5 (present-path facts and history fact) sits uncommitted through Task 6 until Task 5C, and Tasks 1+2's work is committed together at 2C. Every marker does sit at a working, tested point (a `*C` task only comes after its paired `*T` tests), so nothing blocks — but if Task 6 fails midway, Tasks 4–5's tested work has no commit boundary. The completed 260 task file uses the same coarser pattern, so this matches house practice rather than deviating from it.

findings.title: MCP tool inputSchema update for the new required parameter is implicit in Task 11
findings.description: Task 11 makes `generateContext` take a required `adoptionStateWrites` argument and adds `contextTools.test.ts` assertions on what `context_build`/`template_preview` pass, but never names the step of adding the parameter to the MCP tool definitions' input schemas (for `context_build` and `template_preview`). A junior AI following the MCP SDK convention used in this file will do it, and an omitted parameter would fail the tests anyway — so this is a clarification suggestion, not a gap.
